atoms.text: Knut is a Bridge Troll from Trollaland. He and his family live under the bridge right across from the Ugly Green Inn, one of the nicest inns in town. There are all sorts of trolls living not only in Trollaland but also in Troller and Trolltown, Trollaland’s two neighbouring cities. There are Tree Trolls, School Trolls, Shopping Trolls, Tea Trolls, Flower Trolls, and the list goes on and on. Bridge Trolls, according to Knut’s father, are some of the most important trolls. He says that without Bridge Trolls, all other trolls would be unable to pass between the cities and society would collapse, or something like that.

Ever since Knut can remember, he and his mother have conducted daily checks on their family bridge to make sure it is in proper working condition. His mother never lets him miss a day, rain or shine. On these daily checks, Knut and his mother determine whether metal is rusting, if screws are loose, whether the paint looks good, and if the poles are well-planted. Every day, they take their checklist and meticulously evaluate the bridge for weaknesses. No repair is too small.

Once, his mother removed a whole family of birds who had moved into the north corner because she was finding too much poo. Under Knut and the careful eye of his mother, their bridge remained one of the most reliable and best-kept bridges in the city. Knut and his family were, needless to say, extremely proud.

Knut’s father, Bjork, had long told stories of the bridge briars, invisible creatures known for destroying bridges. Rumour has it that hundreds of bridges over the years had been thus destroyed, though thankfully none of them in Trollaland. Knut’s mother, Rolanda, thought these stories were myths. She thought the other trolls were simply not diligent enough and failed to make timely repairs. “Serves those trolls right for not taking enough care!” she would say to Knut’s father after a new report of bridge briars. “Such a thing could never happen to us. We would immediately see the problem and fix it before it got so out of hand. Each troll is responsible for making their own best bridge. We all start on equal footing!”

Knut thought she sounded a little scared. But bridges were her whole life, and it’s not easy to think about things like that.

end.text: This story is told in the 3rd person. You know this because the story is told from the perspective of an outside narrator. This narrator refers to the characters by name or by the third-person pronouns “he”, “she”, or “they”.

atoms.a: Who is the main character of this story?
Why are Knut and his family proud?
b: They are the creators of Bridge Trolls.
They live in a beautiful city.

atoms.a: What do you think the word meticulously in the second paragraph means?
What is Rolanda’s attitude about the bridge briars?
b: She thinks they’re terribly scary and hopes they don’t attack her bridge.
She thinks they’re real but doesn’t worry about them attacking her bridge.
++She doesn’t think they’re real. She thinks other trolls should take better care of their bridges.
